extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: A comprehensive multi-modal evaluation benchmark for multimodal large language models in video analysis, consisting of 900 manually collected and curated videos and 2,700 multiple-choice QA pairs across 6 domains and 30 fine-grained categories.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed in three main steps: video collection, question-answer annotation, and quality review. Videos were manually collected and curated from YouTube across 6 domains and 30 fine-grained categories, with subtitles and audio tracks obtained when available. Annotators then created multiple-choice QA pairs by watching each video and writing three questions per video, followed by a manual review by a different annotator and filtering with Gemini 1.5 Pro to remove questions answerable from text alone.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: 744 videos have subtitles; all 900 videos have audio. The paper notes that subtitles are provided if available, implying some videos lack subtitles.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos were sourced from YouTube, along with corresponding subtitles (if provided) and audio tracks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions that could be answered solely from the text-only question were filtered out. QA pairs were returned to the original annotator for revision if language was unclear, options were not logically consistent, or the correct answer was not appropriate.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Expert annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning manually created multiple-choice QA pairs after thoroughly viewing each video. Each annotator wrote three relevant questions per video, each with four candidate options. A different annotator manually reviewed each QA pair for clarity, logical consistency, and correctness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports that Gemini 1.5 Pro achieved less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup used for filtering, and that option choices were near-uniformly distributed (A/B/C/D: 25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%) to ensure unbiased evaluation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators had strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro was used to filter out QA pairs that could be answered solely from the textual questions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to advance evaluation of multimodal LLMs for video understanding and highlights the need for better handling of long-context and multimodal data.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is described as having a relatively balanced distribution of video durations and a near-uniform distribution of answer options to reduce bias. It also spans 6 domains and 30 categories to improve generalizability.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited by declining model performance on longer videos, sparse frame sampling for long videos in some evaluation settings, and the fact that most open-source models do not support audio input. The paper also notes that long videos are more challenging and that subtitles may be unavailable for some videos.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation benchmark for testing, validation, and comparative assessment of multimodal LLMs in video understanding; also used to analyze the effects of subtitles, audio, and video duration.
